advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct test asserting `attest.sign_plan_review` (and `refresh_attestation`) raises `SigningError` naming the null verified-at-sha refusal when `current_code_sha()` returns falsy.
evidence: attest.py:126-131: `if not current_code_sha(): raise SigningError("refusing to sign a plan-review attestation with no attested snapshot (verified_at_sha would be None)...")`
Comment at attest.py:123-125 asserts this is enforced "at this single seam so every signer ... inherits it" — making it the load-bearing check.
tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py:48-50: monkeypatch changed to `lambda: "c" * 40` (was `lambda: None`), avoiding the branch rather than asserting it.
tests/unit/test_enrich_queue.py:119-121: monkeypatch `current_code_sha` to `"c"*40` to avoid the refusal.

tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py:1663-1667: the only direct `attest.sign_plan_review` refusal test runs after `_commit` (real sha) and asserts only the non-PASS/degraded refusal, not the null-sha refusal.
ABSENCE: `search_files` for "no attested snapshot" in tests returned no matches — no test asserts the null-verified-at-sha SigningError message/branch.
The local-source integration tests reach the __init__.py `source_mode == "local"` guard (sets unsigned signature) BEFORE `sign_plan_review` runs, so they do not exercise the seam.
advisory.finding: The seam-level no-null-pin invariant (attest.py:126 — `if not current_code_sha(): raise SigningError(...)`), described as the single enforcement point every signer inherits, has no test that exercises its failing branch. The two unit tests that previously reached this seam were changed to monkeypatch `current_code_sha` to a real value (test_plan_review_resign.py:50 went from `lambda: None` to `lambda: 'c'*40`; test_enrich_queue.py:121 sets the same), steering AWAY from the guard; the integration tests short-circuit at the higher-level `source_mode == "local"` guard in __init__.py before `sign_plan_review` is called. A future change removing the seam check would leave every test in this diff green.
scenarios: A refactor deletes or weakens the attest.py:126 null-sha guard while keeping the __init__.py source_mode guard — no test in the diff fails, yet a non-local caller that signs with a null current_code_sha could again mint a null-pin attestation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that monkeypatches `rebar.llm.config.current_code_sha` to return None and asserts `pytest.raises(SigningError, match="no attested snapshot")` for both `attest.sign_plan_review(...)` and `attest.refresh_attestation(...)`, complementing the existing non-PASS/degraded refusal test.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no pre-fix local-source REVIEW_RESULT sidecars with source=None exist in live stores that could be recovered via sign-review, or document why the legacy-None tolerance is safe.
evidence: resign.py:106 (diff): `if payload.get("source") == "local":` — only an EXPLICIT 'local' is refused.
sidecar.py:601-607 comment: 'None on legacy payloads (emitted before this field existed) ... resign treats only an explicit "local" as refusing.'
The old (buggy) code signed local-source PASS reviews, so a legacy sidecar from a local review carries verdict=PASS + source absent (None) and would pass this guard.
dropped.finding: resign's local-source refusal treats a `source` of None (legacy sidecars predating the field) as attested-by-default, so a pre-fix local-source review whose sidecar was written before the `source` field existed — which under the buggy old code recorded a signable PASS from a dirty worktree — can still be recovered by `rebar sign-review` into a signed attestation. The recovered attestation is now pinned to an attested basis (so no longer minted from dirty state), but the recovery of a review that was performed against an uncommitted checkout is silently permitted.
